name: Chicken Feed Amount Calculator
seoTitle: Chicken Feed Amount Calculator — Formula & Results
seoDesc: Feed is the largest running cost of a flock, and a laying hen eats roughly 110–120 g a day. Free chicken feed amount calculator: enter your values and get fee
summary:
Feed is the largest running cost of a flock, and a laying hen eats roughly 110–120 g a day. It returns feed per day, total feed, 25 kg bags and feed cost, and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator turns birds, daily intake and a period into kilos of feed, bags and cost. Every result is derived from the boxes you fill in, so changing one input updates the whole panel at once. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Chicken Feed Amount
sections.html:
Total feed (kg) = birds × grams per bird per day × days ÷ 1000

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
birdsnumber of birdsbirds
intakefeed eaten by one bird in a dayg/day
dayslength of the perioddays
totalfeed needed for the periodkg

sections.title: How do I use the Chicken Feed Amount?
sections.html:
The form asks only for what the formula needs — nothing is optional decoration.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: number of birds of 12, feed price of 0.6 per kg.

Substituting them into the formula gives feed per day of 1.44 kg, total feed of 43.2 kg, 25 kg bags of 1.73, feed cost of 25.92, number of days of 30, feed per bird per day of 120 g.

The arithmetic is the page's own: change one box and the result moves by the amount the formula implies, which is the quickest way to convince yourself the tool is honest.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
A raw figure only means something next to the bands it is normally judged against. Here is the scale that goes with this one:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
100 – 130 g/dayLaying hentypical layer intake at 18–20 °C
150 – 200 g/dayBroiler, finishingfast-growing meat birds near market weight
80 – 100 g/dayPullet or bantamsmaller body, lower intake

  • Add 5–10% for spillage and wild birds; feeding to exactly the calculated figure leaves a trough empty before the next delivery.

  • Intake rises with body weight and falls with ambient temperature above about 20 °C, so a winter month and a summer month are not the same calculation.

  • The 25 kg bag count is rounded up in the field: half a bag is a bag you have to buy.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
The arithmetic is simple; the inputs are where things go wrong. The usual culprits:

  • Entering the bag weight instead of the daily intake per bird.
  • Forgetting that chicks eat a fraction of adult intake and that the figure changes weekly.
  • Budgeting for feed without a wastage allowance — usually the difference between the plan and the invoice.

faq.q: How much feed does a chicken eat a day?
faq.a: A laying hen eats about 110–120 g, a broiler 100 g at the start of the cycle rising to 180–200 g at finishing, and a bantam 80–90 g.

faq.q: How many 25 kg bags is that?
faq.a: The calculator divides the total by 25 for you. Order the next whole bag up.

faq.q: What does the Chicken Feed Amount actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns feed per day, total feed, 25 kg bags and feed cost. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
